description: GROUPING() with MULTIPLE arguments returns an integer BITMASK, the first argument being the most significant bit, each bit 1 when that column is aggregated over (rolled up) and 0 when grouped by. Previously a multi-argument call collapsed to a single 0/1 - and always 1, since the 'a, b' argument matched no key. Over ROLLUP(region, product) the detail rows are 0, the region subtotals 1 and the grand total 3. A single argument still yields 0 or 1, and it is 1 exactly when that column's value is NULL. Argument matching is case-INSENSITIVE, so GROUPING(REGION) matches GROUP BY region. Converted 1:1 from query/GroupingBitmaskTest (now retired); the Java counted rows by bitmask and checked a per-row relationship, which the converted tests state as whole ordered row sets - so the bitmask is pinned to the row it belongs to rather than to a tally.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, product VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
SELECT region, product, GROUPING(region, product) AS grp FROM sales GROUP BY ROLLUP(region, product) ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, product NULLS LAST
CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, product VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
SELECT region, product, GROUPING(region) AS gr, GROUPING(product) AS gp FROM sales GROUP BY ROLLUP(region, product) ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, product NULLS LAST
CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, product VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
SELECT region, GROUPING(REGION) AS gr FROM sales GROUP BY ROLLUP(region) ORDER BY region NULLS LAST
